title: Area of an Ellipse Derived via Trig Substitution
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the area enclosed by the ellipse x^2/a^2 + y^2/b^2 = 1.

steps.title: Formulate Quadrant Area Integral
steps.mathExpression: y = b \sqrt{1 - \frac{x^2}{a^2}} = \frac{b}{a}\sqrt{a^2 - x^2} \implies A = 4 \frac{b}{a} \int_0^a \sqrt{a^2 - x^2} dx
steps.explanation: By symmetry, full area is 4 times the first quadrant.

steps.title: Substitute x = a sin(theta)
steps.mathExpression: x = a\sin(\theta) \implies dx = a\cos(\theta) d\theta; \quad x = 0 \implies \theta = 0, \; x = a \implies \theta = \pi/2
steps.explanation: Limits transform from [0, a] to [0, pi/2].

steps.title: Evaluate Integral
steps.explanation: Integral of cos^2 over [0, pi/2] is pi/4.
